In other than Celtic countries surnames have most frequently originated from nicknames descriptive of the personal peculiarities of some early ancestor. Thus in England we find families bearing such names as White, Black, Short, Long, etc. ;

It is certainly not the fact that descriptive nicknames were uncommon amongst the Celts. On the contrary, the quick fancy of this race has always displayed itself in the readiness with which sobriquets of this kind were invented. Isle of Man are usually found near old ecclesiastical sites, as the holy recluses would naturally build their keeills near springs, where they would construct wells both for their own personal convenience as well as for baptizing their disciples.
